posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Its telling that Christopher wrote that they went "their separate ways" instead of "EACH their separate ways". And yes, he's exactly the type of person who would choose his words that carefully.

 

My guess is that Setback and Expatriette went off to have adventures together (maybe thats why we have the "Lucky shot" series). 

Fixer probably went off to center himself and figure out what he was going to do (possibly running up against the Operative again)

Lillian probably went to (or finished) college.  She was a teenager, so the timing seems like it could work for her to spend 4-5 years in college, then another few studying magic, traveling, and getting into trouble. 

Nightmist... I don't know.  Foote has laid out some very, very good arguments for her turning into the miststorm.  Its also possible that she has been corrupted by the curse and is now bad, or she has assumed a more teaching role somewhere, now that the mists are their own thing (IE the miststorm)

 

As for the loss of the ally...

I think that something happened to Parse.  Either she is dead, or uploaded her brain (losing part of her humanity in the process), or betrayed the team in some fashion. 

We know that Parse was involved with the Citizens (Critical multiplier), the organization (arrows in the Operative's back and other cards), Spite (snap decision), skinwalker gloomy (updated intel shows the altar on gloomy's character card), Ambuscade (who was hunting Setback), Revocorp (she worked for them), Revenant (part of revocorp, and she fought Revenant)... Pretty much every single enemy of each member of Dark Watch is represented.  

If she died, or was enslaved, or became a quasi-sentient computer, or a brain in a jar, or turned out to be a villain- that would really screw with the team.

posts.name: Blossercubbles
posts.cooked:
I'll guess that Matriarch played a pivotal role in both the appearance of (even if she was mostly unaware of the fact) and the ultimate defeat or removal of Progeny. If she helped with his (its?) defeat in any way, she'd have the praise she's always yearned for after all these years and could stand shoulder to shoulder with dear cousin Tachyon, which would very likely help her turn into Pinion, alongside NightMist going up to her soon after Progeny shenanigans to help her along the way. 

Control over a human, however, seems very likely to end badly in one way or another. It seems quite possible that Pinion will take this too far at some point as her next major story arc. Regardless, I'm sure Expatriette has contingency plans for her new fellow. She's not a stupid woman, and I'd imagine rather shrewd, what with her mother and all.

Here's hoping that we do manage to see Pinion in action in the Sentinels card game! If not in the final expansion, than maybe as a bonus Mini-Expansion after things wrap up. I can see the series continuing after its conclusion with further mini-expansions, really. No more boxes, but the occasional little wrap-up set? Eh?

I can say that I had become quite fond of the name Nevermore, however. IT seemed like such a great concluding statement for her new bio. Imagine: As  she looked upon her newfound friends, bloodied and battered after their seemingly endless fight against the Master and His Progeny, Lillian Corvus knew she would do evil deeds...Nevermore.

It's cute, right?

posts.cooked:
His henchmen little more than children...

 

I get that Pike grew "clones" for lack of a better word, but what I'm struggling with is why.

 

The Chairman in Sentinels was a mastermind, but his "power" was almost entirely reliant on Talent. The organization sought out individuals of talent to form a near impregnable power base. The Deputy, The Fence, The Muscle, The Contract, The Informant, The Operative. Pike relied on intelligent people, people who could understand how the whole relied on the parts.

 

Now he's growing superpowered infants to work for him. Why?

 

My best guess is that he feels he was betrayed. That's why his madness is taking this shape. Perhaps the Operative left Pike to save herself, as did many of his people. If he feels lack of loyalty caused his downfall raising individuals directly and ruling with an iron fist might be his next tack. He didn't fail he was let down and now that can never happen again.

Exemplar holds himself to be the shining example of how man creates his own success. Hurdles and setbacks only exist to make the ultimate man even stronger. Graham Pike has left the trappings of the average person behind in exchange for perfection. Normal human morality and mortality are obsolete in the face of the works of a true visionary.

posts.cooked:
Christopher:
So it sounds like Exemplar and his minions are going to the be the sole villains of Broken City. Could that mean instead of three seperate scenario books there is just one big scenario book? I'm really interested in figuring out who the 12 playable characters are going to be. We're haven't heard about any other villains besides the goon squad and the box art seems to support this.
Maaaaayyybeeeeeee?

Well, on the villain side:

We have Exemplar 

 

We have Spite, in the various drug-fueled incarnations. 

I'm guessing that it is a singular character with 5 different "modes" according to which drug he is using.  1 mind, 5 bodies. Possibly even the original spirit of spite possessing the clones. could be 5 different characters, with different powers.  

 

I'm guessing that there will be at least 1 other villain, making it comparable to the core game.  We've seen Revenant (at least I strongly suspect it is) lurking at the end of the core game, so I wouldn't be surprised to see Revocorp making a bid for control.  Given the Spite connection, Gloomweaver or a more mystical villain (possibly the cult of Gloomweaver? Will the cursed Acolyte finally be the villain we all know he is?) is also a strong possibility.  Another possibility would be remnants from whatever horrific event happened to break the city (aliens, demons, etc, etc).  

So that is 3-4 playable characters. 

 

On the hero side:

We have Dark Watch, with all 4 members.  that brings us to 7 (or 8 depending on the villains).  

 

Wildcards:

We have green energy girl, who I supect might be The Dreamer.  She had a signifigantly different upbringing from the Visionary, so I wouldn't be surprised if her powerset was substantially different.  Maybe reality alteration?  Could be a hero, could be a villain, could be both depending on how in control of her nightmares she is!

We have Nightmist, who is suspiciously absent.  I wouldn't be surprised to see her make an appearance, possibly as a wildcard- sometimes a villain when her curse is in control, sometimes a hero.  

Has Plague Rat broken Revocorp control and gone back to lurking in the shadows of Rook City? I wouldn't be surprised!

We know that Zhu Long makes a return at some point (given that Fixer is fighting him in a comic that mentions the dragon's return)- we could see Zhu Long's ninjas, or the Dragon himself (itself?).  This seems like a longshot to me, but a possibility nonetheless.  

Thiago wants to be a hero, and we know that he lived in Rook City. If any place needed a hero, Broken City is it.  We have a self-made madman- maybe we'll see a self-made hero leading the orphans of Broken City in response.  

 

Time will tell!
